headline: With the Jev confidence gate, Haiku agents passed A 11/12 vs B 12/12 on 6 blind-query tasks x 2 reps, but B cost 43% more tokens (8.84M -> 12.68M, 120 -> 173 model turns); no case worse. The extra turns were mostly agents waiting on a helper that took 100-300 s on a loaded machine (18 of 24 calls hit the 120 s Bash timeout), the gate fired on n5 r1/r2 and n6 r2 but saved nothing, and Jev never changed the useful #1. Top suggestion: make --provider none (codemap order) the default and keep Jev behind a flag.

arms.name: Plain Claude + unranked candidate list (same codemap pool, raw order, top 10)
Claude + codebase-task-explorer with Jev confidence gate (top-1 p < 0.5 -> warning + 3 rows)
arms.engineVersion: typesafe/jev via OpenRouter decisions API, advisory ranking

evaluation.datasetVersion: tasks-new.json (6 tasks, blind queries); repo copy of 92aa80d with answer-key files removed
evaluation.tokenScope: all tokens of each case agent's session (input + output + cache read + cache write), from its subagent transcript
deviations: Machine under heavy load: about 15 sessions ran at the same time, so helper calls took 100-300 s (15 s alone) in both arms. Checked in the transcripts (evidence/helper-seen.json): the helper output reached 11/12 B agents and only 9/12 A agents (n4 r1, n5 r1, n6 r1 A did not get it). n6 r1 B's helper timed out at 300 s (exit null, no output) and that agent searched on its own. Waiting on the helper adds turns and tokens in both arms, unevenly.

The pass-rate gap is partly noise: n3 r1 A failed with the gold file at its #1 (agent did not read it), and the helper output reached only 9/12 A agents. A scoring-format fix (backslash separators in the answer header) was applied after seeing one such answer (n6 r1 A: Windows-style paths under the skill folder); it applies to both arms and moved A from 10/12 to 11/12.

The gate constants (0.5 / 0.9 / 5 rows / 3 rows) were chosen from the 12 runs of the previous experiment on the same 6 tasks; this run cannot calibrate them (in-sample). Marked PROVISIONAL in code and SKILL.md.
A stray agent was started with the prompt 'PLACEHOLDER' by mistake (it did nothing and touched no file); the real n4 r1 A ran afterwards in its own work folder.
n4 r2 B ran the helper twice (the second time with --no-gate, by the agent's own choice); both runs are in the logs.

The gate result is not part of the helper logs (the helper logs the jev block); the gate decision is derived from jev.global.order[0].p (low on n5 r1/r2 and n6 r2, high on the other cases; n6 r1 B no output).
Arm A contamination check: subagent_usage.mjs --forbid found 0 forbidden calls in all 12 A runs.
Scoring rule from the baseline (relative path counts when the answer names the gold's top folder) applies to both arms.

Independent review (Opus) of the gate diff: 2 Major (thresholds are in-sample; gate not in runs.jsonl) — the second fixed in 92aa80d, the first accepted for this run and marked provisional; Minor findings partly fixed, rest open.
Repo copies and work folders were under D:/cte3 (short path), outside the repo; the helper's .codemap/ cache was written into each copy.
Staleness note: summary.json/report.html were rebuilt after the score fix; helper logs do not contain the rules order or gate field.
